content: Each interaction is described in detail, maintaining the original meaning and context. 1. Nitrofurantoin and Pyridoxine (Antidote): Nitrofurantoin reduces the levels or effects of pyridoxine by altering the intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown but considered minor. 2. Nitrofurantoin and Thiamine: Nitrofurantoin decreases the levels or effects of thiamine by altering the intestinal flora. This interaction is specific to the oral forms of both drugs. The clinical significance is unknown but likely minor. 3. Acalabrutinib and Nitrofurantoin: Acalabrutinib increases the levels of nitrofurantoin by inhibiting intestinal BCRP (Breast Cancer Resistance Protein). Close monitoring is recommended, and caution should be exercised. 4. Aluminum Hydroxide and Nitrofurantoin: Aluminum hydroxide reduces the levels of nitrofurantoin by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. To minimize the interaction, separate administration by at least 2 hours. Monitor closely. 5. Apalutamide and Nitrofurantoin: Apalutamide decreases the levels or effects of nitrofurantoin by increasing its elimination. Apalutamide weakly induces BCRP, potentially reducing systemic exposure to BCRP substrates. Use caution and monitor closely. 6. Nitrofurantoin and Balsalazide: Nitrofurantoin reduces the levels or effects of balsalazide by altering the intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance is unknown but likely minor. 7. Nitrofurantoin and Bazedoxifene/Conjugated Estrogens: Nitrofurantoin decreases the levels or effects of these hormones by altering the intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormones. There is a low risk of contraceptive failure. Use caution and monitor closely. 8. Nitrofurantoin and BCG Vaccine (Live): Nitrofurantoin reduces the effects of the BCG vaccine through pharmacodynamic antagonism. This combination is contraindicated. Live bacterial vaccines should not be administered until antibiotic therapy is completed. 9. Nitrofurantoin and Biotin: Nitrofurantoin decreases the levels or effects of biotin by altering the intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance is unknown but likely minor. 10. Nitrofurantoin and Bupivacaine Implant: Co-administration may increase the toxicity of either drug due to the risk of methemoglobinemia. Monitor closely and use caution. 11. Calcium Carbonate and Nitrofurantoin: Calcium carbonate reduces the levels of nitrofurantoin by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Separate administration by at least 2 hours and monitor closely. 12. Nitrofurantoin and Cholera Vaccine: Nitrofurantoin reduces the effects of the cholera vaccine through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid co-administration with systemic antibiotics, as they may inactivate the vaccine strain. Do not administer the vaccine within 14 days of antibiotic use. 13. Nitrofurantoin and Conjugated Estrogens: Nitrofurantoin decreases the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens by altering the intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormones. There is a low risk of contraceptive failure. Use caution and monitor closely. 14. Danicopan and Nitrofurantoin: Danicopan increases the levels or effects of nitrofurantoin by inhibiting BCRP. Consider dose reduction of BCRP substrates and monitor closely. 15. Nitrofurantoin and Dapsone (Topical): Nitrofurantoin increases the toxicity of dapsone by altering its metabolism, potentially inducing methemoglobinemia. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 16. Darolutamide and Nitrofurantoin: Darolutamide increases the levels or effects of nitrofurantoin by inhibiting BCRP. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, monitor closely and consider dose adjustments. 17. Didanosine and Nitrofurantoin: Didanosine increases the levels or effects of nitrofurantoin by raising gastric pH. This interaction applies to didanosine chewable tablets and oral solutions. Administer nitrofurantoin 2 hours before or several hours after didanosine. Monitor closely. 18. Nitrofurantoin and Digoxin: Nitrofurantoin increases the levels or effects of digoxin by altering the intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. 19. Eluxadoline and Nitrofurantoin: Eluxadoline increases the levels of nitrofurantoin by decreasing its metabolism. Monitor closely and use caution. 20. Enasidenib and Nitrofurantoin: Enasidenib increases the levels or effects of nitrofurantoin by inhibiting BCRP. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, reduce the dosage of BCRP substrates and monitor closely. 21. Estradiol and Nitrofurantoin: Nitrofurantoin decreases the levels or effects of estradiol by altering the intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. There is a low risk of contraceptive failure. Use caution and monitor closely. 22. Fostemsavir and Nitrofurantoin: Fostemsavir inhibits BCRP transporters, increasing the levels or effects of nitrofurantoin. Avoid co-administration or adjust the dose of BCRP substrates. Monitor closely. 23. Glecaprevir/Pibrentasvir and Nitrofurantoin: This combination increases the levels of nitrofurantoin by decreasing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 24. Lasmiditan and Nitrofurantoin: Lasmiditan inhibits BCRP, increasing the levels or effects of nitrofurantoin. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 25. Lenolisib and Nitrofurantoin: Lenolisib, a BCRP inhibitor, increases the systemic exposure of nitrofurantoin. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 26. Magnesium Compounds (Chloride, Citrate, Hydroxide, Oxide, Sulfate) and Nitrofurantoin: These compounds reduce the levels of nitrofurantoin by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance is unknown but likely minor. 27. Nitrofurantoin and Mestranol: Nitrofurantoin decreases the levels or effects of mestranol by altering the intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. There is a low risk of contraceptive failure. Use caution and monitor closely. 28. Metoclopramide and Nitrofurantoin: Metoclopramide reduces the levels of nitrofurantoin by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance is unknown but likely minor. 29. Nitrofurantoin and Microbiota Oral: Nitrofurantoin reduces the effects of microbiota oral products through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid co-administration. Complete antibiotic regimens 2–4 days before initiating microbiota oral therapy. 30. Mipomersen and Nitrofurantoin: Co-administration may increase the toxicity of either drug due to their potential to elevate hepatic enzymes. Monitor liver function tests (LFTs) closely. 31. Momelotinib and Nitrofurantoin: Momelotinib, a BCRP inhibitor, increases the toxicity of nitrofurantoin by competing for plasma protein binding. Adjust the dose of BCRP substrates if necessary and monitor closely. 32. Oxybutynin (Oral, Topical, Transdermal) and Nitrofurantoin: Oxybutynin increases the levels of nitrofurantoin through an unspecified mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. 33. Pantothenic Acid and Nitrofurantoin: Nitrofurantoin decreases the levels or effects of pantothenic acid by altering the intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance is unknown but likely minor. 34. Pexidartinib and Nitrofurantoin: Pexidartinib increases the risk of hepatotoxicity. Avoid co-administration with other hepatotoxic agents. Monitor closely. 35. Ponatinib and Nitrofurantoin: Ponatinib increases the levels of nitrofurantoin through an unspecified mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. 36. Pretomanid and Nitrofurantoin: Co-administration increases the toxicity of either drug. Pretomanid is associated with hepatotoxicity. Avoid alcohol and hepatotoxic agents during therapy. 37. Regorafenib and Nitrofurantoin: Regorafenib inhibits BCRP, increasing the levels or effects of nitrofurantoin. Adjust the dose of BCRP substrates if necessary and monitor closely. 38. Safinamide and Nitrofurantoin: Safinamide inhibits intestinal BCRP, increasing the levels or effects of nitrofurantoin. Monitor for pharmacologic or adverse effects of BCRP substrates. 39. Selinexor and Nitrofurantoin: Selinexor increases the risk of neurological toxicities. Avoid co-administration with medications that cause dizziness or confusion. 40. Sodium Bicarbonate and Nitrofurantoin: Sodium bicarbonate reduces the levels of nitrofurantoin by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. Separate administration by at least 2 hours and monitor closely. 41. Sodium Citrate/Citric Acid and Nitrofurantoin: This combination reduces the levels of nitrofurantoin by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. Separate administration by at least 2 hours and monitor closely. 42. Sodium Picosulfate/Magnesium Oxide/Anhydrous Citric Acid and Nitrofurantoin: Nitrofurantoin reduces the effects of this combination by altering colonic bacterial flora needed for drug activation. Monitor closely. 43. Sofosbuvir/Velpatasvir and Nitrofurantoin: Velpatasvir inhibits BCRP, increasing the levels or effects of nitrofurantoin. Monitor closely and use caution. 44. Stiripentol and Nitrofurantoin: Stiripentol inhibits BCRP, increasing the levels or effects of nitrofurantoin. Adjust the dose of BCRP substrates if adverse effects occur. 45. Tafamidis (and Tafamidis Meglumine) and Nitrofurantoin: Tafamidis inhibits BCRP, increasing the levels or effects of nitrofurantoin. Adjust the dose of BCRP substrates if necessary and monitor closely. 46. Tetracaine and Nitrofurantoin: Co-administration may increase the risk of methemoglobinemia. Monitor for signs of this condition and use caution.
